parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$X\in\{2,3,4,5,6\}$ [B1]
Guidance: Give the correct $X$ values and at least one linked probability. Additional values are allowed only when assigned probability zero.
$P(X=2,3,4)=\frac{1,4,10}{36}$ [B1]
Guidance: Award when three probabilities are correct and linked to their correct outcomes; accept 3 significant figure decimals.
$P(X=5,6)=\frac{12,9}{36}$ [B1]
Guidance: Award for the other two correct linked probabilities; accept 3 significant figure decimals. If fewer than three probabilities are correct, special-case B1 is available for five probabilities strictly between zero and one that sum to one.
Total: 3

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$E(X)=\frac{1(2)+4(3)+10(4)+12(5)+9(6)}{36}$ [M1]
Guidance: Accept an unsimplified expectation expression. Follow through a part (a) table having at least four probabilities strictly between zero and one whose total lies from $0.999$ to $1$.
$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\frac{1(2^2)+4(3^2)+10(4^2)+12(5^2)+9(6^2)}{36}-[E(X)]^2$ [M1]
Guidance: Use an appropriate variance formula subtracting the square of the candidate’s expectation. Follow through a table with at least three probabilities strictly between zero and one; they need not sum to one.
$E(X)=\frac{14}{3}=4.67,\quad \operatorname{Var}(X)=\frac{10}{9}=1.11$ [A1]
Guidance: Both expectation and variance must be identified. The expectation may be identified through correct use in the variance. If no method mark is earned, special-case B1 is available for both identified correct final answers.
Total: 3
